Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Runtime & Deployment

- **Entrypoint**: `bin/serve` prepares SQLite (`bin/rails db:prepare`), compiles Propshaft assets (`bin/rails assets:clobber assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground listening on `0.0.0.0:${PORT}`.
- **Plain HTTP & Host Independence**: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, `config.hosts.clear`, `config.public_file_server.enabled = true`, and ActionCable's `allow_same_origin_as_host = true` ensure the app works over plain HTTP on any conference network hostname without external dependencies.
- **Storage & Concurrency**: All persistent state lives under `storage/` (`storage/production.sqlite3`, WAL mode with `foreign_keys = ON`). `config/database.yml` sizes `max_connections` to `RAILS_MAX_THREADS + 10` so Puma threads (`5`) and ActionCable worker pool threads never starve under conference load.
- **Health Check**: `GET /up` returns `200` without authentication.

## Authentication & Authorization

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic Authentication comparing against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]` using SHA-256 digests with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. Empty credentials are always rejected (`401`).
- Public player routes (`/play/:code`, `/play/:code/join`, `/play/:code/answer`, `/play/:code/state`) inherit directly from `ApplicationController` and require no account or moderator credentials.
- ActionCable channels authorize per-channel via Rails `ActiveRecord::SignedId` tokens with distinct purposes (`:moderator_channel` on `Game`, `:player_channel` on `Player`) so players cannot subscribe to moderator streams or other players' streams.

## Data Model

### Quiz Authoring
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required, whitespace-normalized). `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `Question` (`questions`): `quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active` (default `true`). `has_many :options, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :game_questions, dependent: :nullify`.
- `Option` (`options`): `question_id`, `title`, `correct` (default `false`), `position`.
- `Question#save_with_options` validates `body` and non-empty option rows (>= 2 options, >= 1 correct) before touching the DB.
- `Question#move!(direction)` atomically swaps adjacent positions and normalizes `1..N`.

### Live Games (Snapshotted per Run)
- `Game` (`games`): `quiz_id`, `code` (unique 5-char uppercase unambiguous code, e.g. `K7RZX`), `status` (`lobby` -> `question` -> `reveal` -> `ended`), `current_question_position`, `started_at`, `ended_at`.
  - `Game.create_for_quiz!(quiz)` snapshots only active questions (in position order) into `GameQuestion` and their options into `GameOption`. Inactive questions are skipped, and later edits/deletes on `Question`/`Option` never break or corrupt past/running games.
  - State transitions (`start!`, `finish_question!`, `next_question!`, `end_game!`) use atomic conditional `update_all` guards (with optional `expected_position`) inside transactions so accidental double-clicks cannot skip questions.
- `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`): `game_id`, `question_id` (nullable, `on_delete: :nullify`), `body`, `position`.
- `GameOption` (`game_options`): `game_question_id`, `title`, `correct`, `position`.
- `Player` (`players`): `game_id`, `name` (whitespace-normalized, duplicate names allowed), `token` (unique random token persisted in a per-game signed HttpOnly cookie `quizzy_player_#{code}` so reopening the join link in the same browser continues as the same player).
- `Answer` (`answers`): `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, unique index on `[player_id, game_question_id]`. `Game#record_answer!` uses `Answer.upsert` so players can change their pick while a question is open and the last pick counts; submissions after `"Finish"` are rejected with `409` and return the authoritative server state.

### Security Invariant (Answer Confidentiality)
- `Game#player_broadcast_state` and `Game#player_state` strictly omit `correct` flags while `status` is `"lobby"` or `"question"`, and only expose the current question's options (never upcoming questions). Neither the initial HTML source, JSON state endpoint, nor WebSocket frames reveal correct answers before `"Finish"`.

## Real-Time Updates, Presence & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience

- **Transport**: ActionCable (`adapter: async` in single-process Puma, `actioncable.esm.js` vendored offline via Importmap) with three channels:
  - `ModeratorGameChannel`: streams `game:#{id}:moderator` (`state`, `presence`, `counts`) and immediately transmits full `moderator_state` on subscribe/reconnect.
  - `PlayerGameChannel`: streams `game:#{id}:players` (shared phase transitions without thundering-herd HTTP refetches on reveal) and `game:#{id}:player:#{player.id}` (",

class GamePresence

  HTTP_FALLBACK_TTL = 6.0

      update_entry(game_id.to_i, player_id.to_i, connection_id.to_s, ttl: ttl)
    end

    def heartbeat(game_id, player_id, connection_id, ttl: STALE_AFTER)
      update_entry(game_id.to_i, player_id.to_i, connection_id.to_s, ttl: ttl)

  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

      return @submitted_option_rows
    end

      options.map { |opt| { title: opt.title, correct: opt.correct } }
    else
      Array.new(DEFAULT_OPTION_ROWS) { { title: "", correct: false } }
    end
  end

  def save_with_options(raw_rows)
    @submitted_option_rows = normalize_submitted_rows(raw_rows)
    non_empty_rows = @submitted_option_rows.reject { |row| row[:title].strip.empty? }

    assign_next_position if position.nil?

    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if non_empty_rows.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if non_empty_rows.none? { |row| row[:correct] }

    return false if errors.any?

    transaction do
      assign_next_position if new_record?
      save!
      options.delete_all
      non_empty_rows.each_with_index do |row, index|
        options.create!(
          title: row[:title].strip,
          correct: row[:correct],
          position: index + 1
        )
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def move!(direction)
    return false unless persisted?

    transaction do
      ordered_questions = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      idx = ordered_questions.index(self)
      return false unless idx

      target_idx =
        case direction.to_s
        when "up" then idx - 1
        when "down" then idx + 1
        else return false
        end

      return false if target_idx.negative? || target_idx >= ordered_questions.length

      ordered_questions[idx], ordered_questions[target_idx] =
        ordered_questions[target_idx], ordered_questions[idx]

      ordered_questions.each_with_index do |question, index|
        new_pos = index + 1
        question.update_column(:position, new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
      end
    end

    true
  end

  private

  def assign_next_position
    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

        raw_rows.to_h.sort_by { |k, _| k.to_i }.map(&:last)
      when Hash

require "rqrcode"

module ApplicationHelper
  def option_letter(index)
    n = index + 1
    result = +""
    while n > 0
      n -= 1
      result.prepend(("A".ord + (n % 26)).chr)
      n /= 26
    end
    result
  end

  def qr_code_svg(content)
    qr = RQRCode::QRCode.new(content.to_s)
    qr.as_svg(
      color: "000000",
      fill: "ffffff",
      shape_rendering: "crispEdges",
      module_size: 6,
      offset: 24,
      standalone: true,
      use_path: true,
      viewbox: true
    ).sub(/\A<\?xml[^?]*\?>\s*/, "")
  end

  def big_screen_cover_class(status)
    case status.to_s
    when "question", "reveal"
      "cover cover--blue cover--calm"
    when "ended"
      "cover cover--night"
    else
      "cover"
    end
  end

require "test_helper"

class GameChannelsTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Channel Security Quiz")
    q = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Is Ruby fun?", active: true)
    assert q.save_with_options([
      { title: "Yes", correct: true },
      { title: "No", correct: false }
    ])
    @game = Game.create_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    @player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
  end

  test "ModeratorGameChannel rejects missing, forged, or player tokens and accepts valid moderator token" do
    self.class.tests ModeratorGameChannel

    subscribe
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(token: "forged-token")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    # Player's signed token must NOT grant access to ModeratorGameChannel
    subscribe(token: @player.stream_token)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(token: @game.moderator_stream_token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream Game.moderator_stream_name(@game.id)
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last["status"]
  end

  test "PlayerGameChannel rejects invalid or moderator tokens, tracks presence, and never leaks correct before reveal" do
    self.class.tests PlayerGameChannel

    subscribe
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(token: @game.moderator_stream_token)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    @game.start!
    subscribe(token: @player.stream_token, tab_id: "tab-a")
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream Game.players_stream_name(@game.id)
    assert_has_stream Game.player_stream_name(@game.id, @player.id)
    assert_equal 1, GamePresence.player_count(@game.id)

    payload = transmissions.last
    assert_equal "question", payload["status"]
    payload["question"]["options"].each do |opt|
      assert_not opt.key?("correct")
    end

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.player_count(@game.id)
  end

  test "JoinStatusChannel streams join status without registering presence" do
    self.class.tests JoinStatusChannel

    subscribe(code: "NOPE1")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(code: @game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream Game.join_status_stream_name(@game.id)
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.player_count(@game.id)
  end
end

Okay, let's break this down systematically. The core task is adding a "Number of winners" setting to quiz configuration.  The first step is figuring out where this new setting will live.  I see that `app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb` handles both new quiz creation and editing existing quizzes, which makes it perfect.  Adding the field here ensures it's available in both contexts, with a default value of 3, as specified.

Next, the model. I need a database column for this. The question is, what to call it: `winners_count` or `number_of_winners`? Let me see... `number_of_winners` aligns perfectly with the English label and will make validation error messages cleaner and more readable.  Good for user experience. Let's see if Rails' humanization feature agrees: `Quiz.human_attribute_name(:number_of_winners)` should give us the label, and it does. Perfect! The database column needs to be an integer, defaulting to 3, and not nullable.  So, I'll need to create a migration: `add_column :quizzes, :number_of_winners, :integer, default: 3, null: false`.

Now, the crucial question: should the game snapshot the number of winners when it's created, or should it read the number of winners live from the quiz?  This has implications for how quiz settings impact running and past games.  I need to consider all scenarios. What if a moderator changes the winner setting *after* a game is started? Or even while a game is running?  What's the expected behavior?

Let's think through the use cases:

*   **Case A:** The user creates a quiz, sets "Number of winners" to 2, and *then* starts a game. Either snapshotting or reading live would result in 2 winners.
*   **Case B:** A test runs a game with 3 winners, finishes it, then later changes the quiz to 5 winners for a second run.  This is the tricky one. Snapshotting keeps the *past* game at 3 winners, while reading live would give the *new* value of 5, which could be confusing.

So, *does* a moderator change settings mid-game?

I am thinking about how a moderator would likely use this: A moderator likely edits quiz settings to the desired number (say, 2) *before* starting the game, and during the game, they just run the quiz. After the game, they click "End Quiz" and see "Top 2".

The decision of snapshot vs. live read depends on whether there are any potential scenarios where a user would expect a change in quiz settings to affect an already-created, running, or viewed game. The architecture documentation says that `Game.create_for_quiz!` snapshots active questions and options to protect past/running games. The *spirit* of the design is to lock game content for consistency over time! Therefore, I will include `number_of_winners: quiz.number_of_winners` when the game is created. This seems best, so a game retains its original settings, even if the quiz is modified later. This makes the most sense.

I'd rather the user get the settings *before* starting the game than expect some kind of dynamic live update. Let's check `moderate/quizzes/show.html.erb` to see whether old games are viewable in the UI! This will help with the final design decision.

**Deep Dive into Quiz Logic and Implementation**

Alright, let's break this down. First, regarding the form validation for the quiz: that HTML5 `<input type="number">` behavior with `min="1"` and/or `required` threw me a curveball, but it actually provides a really elegant solution to validation. It cleanly handles scenarios where a QA test tries to submit a value of `0`, `-1`, or an empty string. The browser's native tooltip handles the rejection without server interaction unless `novalidate` is present. And using the `novalidate` attribute allows for comprehensive testing of both browser-side and server-side validation using Rails. The Rails validation of the `number_of_winners` field, with `presence: true` and `numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1, allow_blank: true }` catches all the invalid inputs. The existing `.input--number` class in the CSS is literally *perfect* for this purpose, it was designed for this exact field! So that part seems pretty robust, especially with how Rails casting handles the numericality, so we're good there. The edge case of resetting the value to `0` during edit mode will get caught by the server-side validation.

Now, about scoring and timing. The crux is capturing the exact moment a question *opens* and when a player's *last* pick is made. I'm going to add that `opened_at` column to `game_questions`, to the millisecond, which also applies in rails 8.1. That ensures accurate time calculation and resolves any ambiguities. That `response_time_us` field directly on the answers, storing the *exact* microseconds, is also critical. A player might switch answers, and we're looking for that last pick. The game logic needs to *always* update the `answered_at` and `response_time_us` if the answer changes; even a retry of the same option needs to have no time penalty. And that check in `player_game_controller.js`, `if (this.desiredOptionId === this.confirmedOptionId) return`, is essential to prevent duplicate calls, preventing a click penalty. And using microsecond precision, both in the DB and with `Time.current`, creates a clean testable story, even with Rails's `travel_to`.

Finally, the leaderboard and winner selection. The ranking is based on correct answers and the time they take. Ties are broken by the *total time of correct* answers. Zero-point players have to be excluded from winner calculations. And, the "place" for each player *has* to be sequential, even with ties, to ensure a deterministic leaderboard. The winner selection is going to be handled by the two buttons, and let's go over the logic to ensure that winner selection is solid.

The "Top N" button is straightforward, so we pick the top `n` players. The "Draw" button is the more complex one, it correctly handles ties, and should be random but *reproducible*. The code has to be super careful:
1. `eligible` includes only players with points.
2. If `eligible.size <= n` (i.e. we don't need to select more winners), then we select all.
3. If `eligible.size > n`, then `cutoff_points` is the `n`-th place points on the eligible players' leaderboard, `auto_winners` are the players above the cutoff. The remainder must be selected randomly using `tied_pool.sample()`.

The button labels, and what to do with them, need to be clear and consistent. "Top N", "Draw", and "Reset winners" have to be always visible and enabled when `status == "ended"` so there is no ambiguity for QA or when using the app. So, that's what I've got, and I'm ready to code.

**Analyzing the Real-Time Broadcast Architecture**

Okay, hold on a minute! I need to *really* focus on how `ActionCable` integrates with these key methods: `end_game!`, `pick_winners!`, and `broadcast_state!`. It's crucial to understand the data flow, especially with the current setup.

My first thought is to dive deep into every broadcast path.

Let's start with the question lifecycle – how the game progresses from being open (`start!`, `next_question!`) to revealed (`finish_question!`).

Right now, in both production and development, we're using the `async` adapter with `ActionCable`. Importantly, our Puma configuration (`config/puma.rb`) is running a single-process Puma with `threads 5, 5`. We're not using clustering. This is important! The `async` adapter runs *in-process*, directly over WebSockets.

So, when the moderator clicks "Start" or "Next" on the interface, here's what happens:

1.  A `POST` request is sent (e.g., `/moderate/games/:id/start` or `/next`).
2.  The server updates the game state in a *single*, fast SQLite transaction:
    *   `games.status` is set to "question"
    *   `current_question_position` is updated
    *   `game_questions.opened_at` is set to the current time.
3.  The server then calls `broadcast_state!`. This is where the magic happens:
    *   `moderator_state` is broadcast to the `game:#{id}:moderator` channel. This means every open big-screen tab gets the updated moderator state immediately. Plus, the HTTP POST response *also* returns `moderator_state` directly to the tab where the moderator clicked!
    *   `player_broadcast_state` is broadcast to the `game:#{id}:players` channel. This goes to *every* connected phone WebSocket, all in the same microsecond loop. It's the *same* frame for everyone.
4.  There's no need for HTTP polling here, which is fantastic! We're eliminating N+1 DB queries per player when a question starts.

**Database Schema and Controller Analysis**

Okay, first things first, let me organize my thoughts. Turbo Drive is handling ActionCable connections cleanly.  `disconnect()` and `connect()` are being called on the appropriate controllers (`moderator_game_controller.js` and `player_game_controller.js`) when the user navigates. Stimulus is correctly managing the lifecycle, which is good. We’re subscribing and unsubscribing cleanly, which is great to see. The ActionCable setup isn't requiring HTTP Basic Auth on `/cable`, thank goodness. We are using Rails `signed_id` for authorization, which is ideal for security.  No need to manage credentials on the client, and we can still support mobile clients this way.

Now, let's dive into the data model and migrations. I need to make sure this is solid.

The plan is to add a `number_of_winners` to the `quizzes` table. *Should* we snapshot that number on the `games` table? Okay, let's break down all the scenarios.

Scenario 1-6 are all covered if we read the `quiz.number_of_winners` directly from the `Quiz` model on the fly.  This matches our existing `quiz.title` pattern which we also read from the `quiz` model directly.  I'll need to remember to check if the `quiz` might be cached in memory on `@game`. Oh, right! `game.reload` clears that association cache (`@association_cache`)! No issues there.

Now, let's consider the `game_questions` table. `opened_at` will be set to `Time.current` when the question opens. That's straightforward.

The `answers` table: a `response_time_us` column is added. Using `response_time_us` (as an `integer`) allows for precise timing and efficient aggregation, and it avoids datetime quirks. Creating separate `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps for `answers` makes sense. `created_at` will be when a player first answers, and `updated_at` reflects their last choice.

Finally, we are adding a `winner` boolean to the `players` table. There's no need for an index on `game_id` on the `players` table. We already have one, and that should be fast enough.

Let's carefully review the `Answer` upsert logic.

`record_answer!` first checks to make sure the game question is actually open.  Then we see if there’s an existing answer. If the player is just re-tapping the same option on a retried request, it preserves the original response time.  If the player changes their mind, it updates the `game_option_id`, `response_time_us`, and `updated_at`. If two concurrent requests come in for different options (same player, two tabs), SQLite will serialize them, which is perfect and `Answer.upsert` with `unique_by` handles it safely. class Game < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question reveal ended].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :answers, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  class << self
    def find_by_code(raw_code)
      normalized = raw_code.to_s.strip.upcase
      return nil if normalized.empty?

      find_by(code: normalized)
    end

    def create_for_quiz!(quiz)
      active_questions = quiz.active_questions.to_a
      return nil if active_questions.empty?

      transaction do
        game = quiz.games.create!(code: generate_unique_code, status: "lobby")
        active_questions.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
          gq = game.game_questions.create!(
            question_id: question.id,
            body: question.body,
            position: q_index + 1
          )
          question.options.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
            gq.game_options.create!(
              title: option.title,
              correct: option.correct?,
              position: o_index + 1
            )
          end
        end
        game
      end
    end

    def moderator_stream_name(game_id)
      "game:#{game_id}:moderator"
    end

    def players_stream_name(game_id)
      "game:#{game_id}:players"
    end

    def player_stream_name(game_id, player_id)
      "game:#{game_id}:player:#{player_id}"
    end

    def join_status_stream_name(game_id)
      "game:#{game_id}:join_status"
    end

    private

    def generate_unique_code
      loop do
        candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join
        return candidate unless exists?(code: candidate)
      end
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question?
    status == "question"
  end

  def reveal?
    status == "reveal"
  end

  def ended?
    status == "ended"
  end

  def number_of_winners
    quiz.number_of_winners
  end

  def total_questions
    @total_questions ||= game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return nil if current_question_position.nil?

    game_questions.includes(:game_options).find_by(position: current_question_position)
  end

  def last_question?
    current_question_position.present? && current_question_position >= total_questions
  end

  def moderator_stream_token
    signed_id(purpose: :moderator_channel, expires_in: 24.hours)
  end

  def start!
    changed = false
    transaction do
      return false unless game_questions.exists?

      now = Time.current
      updated = self.class.where(id: id, status: "lobby").update_all(
        [
          "status = ?, current_question_position = ?, started_at = ?, updated_at = ?, state_version = state_version + 1",
          "question", 1, now, now
        ]
      )
      if updated == 1
        game_questions.where(position: 1).update_all(opened_at: now, updated_at: now)
        changed = true
      end
    end

    reload
    @total_questions = nil
    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def finish_question!(expected_position: nil)
    changed = false
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question?
      return false if expected_position.present? && current_question_position != expected_position.to_i

      now = Time.current
      updated = self.class.where(
        id: id,
        status: "question",
        current_question_position: current_question_position
      ).update_all(
        [
          "status = ?, updated_at = ?, state_version = state_version + 1",
          "reveal", now
        ]
      )
      changed = updated == 1
    end

    reload
    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def next_question!(expected_position: nil)
    changed = false
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless reveal? && !last_question?
      return false if expected_position.present? && current_question_position != expected_position.to_i

      from_pos = current_question_position
      next_pos = from_pos + 1
      now = Time.current
      updated = self.class.where(
        id: id,
        status: "reveal",
        current_question_position: from_pos
      ).update_all(
        [
          "status = ?, current_question_position = ?, updated_at = ?, state_version = state_version + 1",
          "question", next_pos, now
        ]
      )
      if updated == 1
        game_questions.where(position: next_pos).update_all(opened_at: now, updated_at: now)
        changed = true
      end
    end

    reload
    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def end_game!
    changed = false
    transaction do
      now = Time.current
      updated = self.class.where(id: id).where.not(status: "ended").update_all(
        [
          "status = ?, ended_at = ?, updated_at = ?, state_version = state_version + 1",
          "ended", now, now
        ]
      )
      changed = updated == 1
    end

    reload
    if changed
      broadcast_state!
      GamePresence.clear_game!(id)
    end
    changed
  end

  def record_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    saved = false
    selected_id = nil
    question_id = nil

    transaction do
      reload
      return { ok: false, state: player_state(player) } unless question?

      q = current_question
      return { ok: false, state: player_state(player) } unless q && q.id == game_question_id.to_i

      option = q.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id)
      return { ok: false, state: player_state(player) } unless option

      now = Time.current
      existing = Answer.find_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: q.id)

      if existing && existing.game_option_id == option.id
        selected_id = option.id
        question_id = q.id
        saved = true
      else
        opened_at = q.opened_at || started_at || now
        elapsed_us = [ ((now.to_r - opened_at.to_r) * 1_000_000).round, 0 ].max

        Answer.upsert(
          {
            game_id: id,
            player_id: player.id,
            game_question_id: q.id,
            game_option_id: option.id,
            response_time_us: elapsed_us,
            created_at: now,
            updated_at: now
          },
          unique_by: %i[ player_id game_question_id ],
          update_only: %i[ game_option_id response_time_us updated_at ]
        )

        selected_id = option.id
        question_id = q.id
        saved = true
      end
    end

    if saved
      broadcast_counts!
      broadcast_player_selection!(player.id, question_id, selected_id)
      { ok: true, game_question_id: question_id, selected_option_id: selected_id }
    else
      { ok: false, state: player_state(player) }
    end
  end

  def leaderboard
    all_players = players.order(:created_at, :id).to_a
    return [] if all_players.empty?

    correct_stats = answers
      .joins(:game_option)
      .where(game_options: { correct: true })
      .group(:player_id)
      .pluck(
        :player_id,
        Arel.sql("COUNT(*)"),
        Arel.sql("COALESCE(SUM(answers.response_time_us), 0)")
      )
      .each_with_object({}) do |(player_id, pts, total_us), map|
        map[player_id] = [ pts.to_i, total_us.to_i ]
      end

    ranked = all_players.map do |player|
      points, total_time_us = correct_stats.fetch(player.id, [ 0, 0 ])
      {
        player_id: player.id,
        name: player.name,
        points: points,
        total_time_us: total_time_us,
        winner: player.winner?,
        created_at: player.created_at
      }
    end

    ranked.sort_by! { |entry| [ -entry[:points], entry[:total_time_us], entry[:created_at], entry[:player_id] ] }

    ranked.each_with_index.map do |entry, idx|
      {
        place: idx + 1,
        player_id: entry[:player_id],
        name: entry[:name],
        points: entry[:points],
        total_time_us: entry[:total_time_us],
        winner: entry[:winner]
      }
    end
  end

  def pick_top_winners!
    entries = nil
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless ended?

      current_entries = leaderboard
      eligible = current_entries.select { |entry| entry[:points].positive? }
      winner_ids = eligible.first(number_of_winners).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }

      apply_winners_locked!(winner_ids)
      winner_set = winner_ids.to_set
      entries = current_entries.map { |entry| entry.merge(winner: winner_set.include?(entry[:player_id])) }
    end

    reload
    broadcast_state!(leaderboard_entries: entries)
    true
  end

  def draw_winners!(random: Random.new)
    entries = nil
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless ended?

      current_entries = leaderboard
      eligible = current_entries.select { |entry| entry[:points].positive? }
      n = number_of_winners

      winner_ids =
        if eligible.size <= n
          eligible.map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
        else
          cutoff_points = eligible[n - 1][:points]
          auto_winners = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] > cutoff_points }
          tied_pool = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }
          remaining = n - auto_winners.size
          drawn = tied_pool.sample(remaining, random: random)
          (auto_winners + drawn).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
        end

      apply_winners_locked!(winner_ids)
      winner_set = winner_ids.to_set
      entries = current_entries.map { |entry| entry.merge(winner: winner_set.include?(entry[:player_id])) }
    end

    reload
    broadcast_state!(leaderboard_entries: entries)
    true
  end

  def reset_winners!
    entries = nil
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless ended?

      current_entries = leaderboard
      apply_winners_locked!([])
      entries = current_entries.map { |entry| entry.merge(winner: false) }
    end

    reload
    broadcast_state!(leaderboard_entries: entries)
    true
  end

  def current_question_answers_count
    q = current_question
    return 0 unless q

    answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count
  end

  def moderator_state(question: nil, leaderboard_entries: nil)
    q = question || current_question
    players_count = GamePresence.player_count(id)

    payload = {
      type: "state",
      state_version: state_version,
      game_id: id,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      number_of_winners: number_of_winners,
      status: status,
      total_questions: total_questions,
      current_question_position: current_question_position,
      is_last_question: last_question?,
      players_count: players_count,
      answers_count: q && (question? || reveal?) ? answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count : 0,
      question: nil,
      leaderboard: []
    }

    if q && (question? || reveal?)
      if reveal?
        counts_by_option = answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).group(:game_option_id).count
        total_answers = counts_by_option.values.sum
        payload[:question] = {
          id: q.id,
          position: q.position,
          total: total_questions,
          body: q.body,
          total_answers: total_answers,
          options: q.game_options.map do |opt|
            count = counts_by_option.fetch(opt.id, 0)
            {
              id: opt.id,
              title: opt.title,
              position: opt.position,
              correct: opt.correct?,
              count: count,
              share: total_answers.positive? ? ((count * 100.0) / total_answers).round : 0
            }
          end
        }
      else
        payload[:question] = {
          id: q.id,
          position: q.position,
          total: total_questions,
          body: q.body,
          options: q.game_options.map do |opt|
            {
              id: opt.id,
              title: opt.title,
              position: opt.position
            }
          end
        }
      end
    elsif ended?
      entries = leaderboard_entries || leaderboard
      payload[:leaderboard] = entries.map do |entry|
        {
          place: entry[:place],
          player_id: entry[:player_id],
          name: entry[:name],
          points: entry[:points],
          winner: entry[:winner]
        }
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  # Public broadcast state sent to all connected players during active phases.
  # STRICT SECURITY INVARIANT:
  # - Never includes `correct` flags while status is "lobby" or "question"!
  # - Never includes points, scores, or places while game is running!
  def player_broadcast_state(question: nil)
    case status
    when "lobby"
      { type: "state", state_version: state_version, status: "lobby" }
    when "question"
      q = question || current_question
      {
        type: "state",
        state_version: state_version,
        status: "question",
        question: q ? {
          id: q.id,
          position: q.position,
          total: total_questions,
          body: q.body,
          options: q.game_options.map do |opt|
            {
              id: opt.id,
              title: opt.title,
              position: opt.position
            }
          end
        } : nil
      }
    when "reveal"
      q = question || current_question
      {
        type: "state",
        state_version: state_version,
        status: "reveal",
        question: q ? {
          id: q.id,
          position: q.position,
          total: total_questions,
          body: q.body,
          options: q.game_options.map do |opt|
            {
              id: opt.id,
              title: opt.title,
              position: opt.position,
              correct: opt.correct?
            }
          end
        } : nil
      }
    else
      { type: "state", state_version: state_version, status: "ended" }
    end
  end

  # Personalized state for a specific player (initial render, WS subscribe resync, HTTP state).
  # STRICT SECURITY INVARIANT:
  # - Never includes `correct` flags before status is "reveal"!
  # - Never includes points/place/winner before status is "ended"!
  def player_state(player, leaderboard_entries: nil)
    payload = player_broadcast_state.merge(player_name: player.name)

    if (question? || reveal?) && (q = current_question)
      answer = answers.includes(:game_option).find_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: q.id)
      payload[:selected_option_id] = answer&.game_option_id

      if reveal?
        payload[:result] =
          if answer.nil?
            "no_answer"
          elsif answer.game_option.correct?
            "correct"
          else
            "wrong"
          end
      end
    elsif ended?
      entries = leaderboard_entries || leaderboard
      entry = entries.find { |item| item[:player_id] == player.id }
      if entry
        payload[:place] = entry[:place]
        payload[:total_players] = entries.size
        payload[:points] = entry[:points]
        payload[:winner] = entry[:winner]
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def broadcast_state!(question: nil, leaderboard_entries: nil)
    if ended?
      entries = leaderboard_entries || leaderboard
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        self.class.moderator_stream_name(id),
        moderator_state(leaderboard_entries: entries)
      )
      broadcast_ended_to_players!(entries)
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        self.class.join_status_stream_name(id),
        { type: "state", state_version: state_version, status: "ended" }
      )
    else
      q = question || current_question
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        self.class.players_stream_name(id),
        player_broadcast_state(question: q)
      )
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        self.class.moderator_stream_name(id),
        moderator_state(question: q)
      )
    end
  end

  def broadcast_presence!(players_count = GamePresence.player_count(id))
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      self.class.moderator_stream_name(id),
      { type: "presence", players_count: players_count }
    )
  end

  def broadcast_counts!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      self.class.moderator_stream_name(id),
      {
        type: "counts",
        answers_count: current_question_answers_count,
        players_count: GamePresence.player_count(id)
      }
    )
  end

  def broadcast_player_selection!(player_id, game_question_id, selected_option_id)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      self.class.player_stream_name(id, player_id),
      {
        type: "selection",
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        selected_option_id: selected_option_id
      }
    )
  end

  private

  def apply_winners_locked!(winner_ids)
    now = Time.current
    if winner_ids.empty?
      players.where(winner: true).update_all(winner: false, updated_at: now)
    else
      players.where(winner: true).where.not(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: false, updated_at: now)
      players.where(id: winner_ids, winner: false).update_all(winner: true, updated_at: now)
    end
    self.class.where(id: id).update_all([ "state_version = state_version + 1, updated_at = ?", now ])
  end

  def broadcast_ended_to_players!(entries)
    total = entries.size
    entries.each do |entry|
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        self.class.player_stream_name(id, entry[:player_id]),
        {
          type: "state",
          state_version: state_version,
          status: "ended",
          place: entry[:place],
          total_players: total,
          points: entry[:points],
          winner: entry[:winner]
        }
      )
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class GameScoringAndWinnersTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveSupport::Testing::TimeHelpers

  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Prizes Talk Quiz", number_of_winners: 3)

    @q1 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Q1?", active: true)
    assert @q1.save_with_options([
      { title: "Q1 Right", correct: true },
      { title: "Q1 Wrong", correct: false }
    ])

    @q2 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Q2?", active: true)
    assert @q2.save_with_options([
      { title: "Q2 Right A", correct: true },
      { title: "Q2 Right B", correct: true },
      { title: "Q2 Wrong", correct: false }
    ])

    @q3 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Q3?", active: true)
    assert @q3.save_with_options([
      { title: "Q3 Right", correct: true },
      { title: "Q3 Wrong", correct: false }
    ])
  end

  test "ranks players by points then lower total time of correct answers, using last pick time and ignoring wrong answer time" do
    base_time = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-20 10:00:00 UTC")
    game = nil
    alice = bob = carol = dave = eve = nil

    travel_to(base_time) do
      game = Game.create_for_quiz!(@quiz)
      alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
      bob   = game.players.create!(name: "Bob")
      carol = game.players.create!(name: "Carol")
      dave  = game.players.create!(name: "Dave")
      eve   = game.players.create!(name: "Eve")

      gq1, gq2, gq3 = game.game_questions.includes(:game_options).to_a
      q1_right = gq1.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q1 Right")
      q1_wrong = gq1.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q1 Wrong")
      q2_right_a = gq2.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q2 Right A")
      q2_right_b = gq2.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q2 Right B")
      q2_wrong = gq2.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q2 Wrong")
      q3_right = gq3.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q3 Right")
      q3_wrong = gq3.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q3 Wrong")

      # Q1 opens at T=0
      assert game.start!
      assert_in_delta base_time.to_f, gq1.reload.opened_at.to_f, 0.001

      # T+1s: Carol picks RIGHT early, Alice picks RIGHT, Dave picks WRONG
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: carol, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      # Duplicate retry of Alice's same pick at T+10s shouldn't happen yet; let's test at T+2s

      # T+2s: Bob picks RIGHT; Alice sends duplicate retry of SAME option (keeps T+1s!)
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)

      # T+3s: Carol changes to WRONG
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: carol, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_wrong.id)

      # T+5s: Carol changes BACK to RIGHT (her Q1 time MUST be 5s, NOT 1s!)
      # Dave picks WRONG slowly at T+5s (wrong answer time must NOT count!)
      travel 2.seconds
      game.record_answer!(player: carol, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      game.record_answer!(player: dave, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_wrong.id)

      # During question & reveal, players must NEVER see points, place, or winner
      [ alice, bob, carol, dave, eve ].each do |p|
        st = game.player_state(p)
        assert_not st.key?(:points)
        assert_not st.key?(:place)
        assert_not st.key?(:total_players)
        assert_not st.key?(:winner)
      end

      game.finish_question!
      [ alice, bob, carol, dave, eve ].each do |p|
        st = game.player_state(p)
        assert_not st.key?(:points)
        assert_not st.key?(:place)
        assert_not st.key?(:total_players)
        assert_not st.key?(:winner)
      end

      # Wait 10 seconds before opening Q2 (proves Q2 timer starts at Q2 open, not Q1 open!)
      travel 10.seconds
      assert game.next_question!
      assert_in_delta Time.current.to_f, gq2.reload.opened_at.to_f, 0.001

      # T_q2 + 0.5s: Dave answers RIGHT (total correct time = 0.5s, 1 pt!)
      travel 0.5.seconds
      game.record_answer!(player: dave, game_question_id: gq2.id, game_option_id: q2_right_b.id)

      # T_q2 + 4s: Alice answers RIGHT (total correct time = 1s + 4s = 5s, 2 pts)
      #            Bob answers WRONG (stays at 1 pt, total correct time = 2s)
      #            Carol answers WRONG (stays at 1 pt, total correct time = 5s)
      travel 3.5.seconds
      game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: gq2.id, game_option_id: q2_right_a.id)
      game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: gq2.id, game_option_id: q2_wrong.id)
      game.record_answer!(player: carol, game_question_id: gq2.id, game_option_id: q2_wrong.id)

      game.finish_question!

      # Q3 opens
      travel 5.seconds
      assert game.next_question!

      # T_q3 + 1s: Bob answers RIGHT (total 2 pts, total correct time = 2s + 1s = 3s -> FASTER than Alice's 5s!)
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: gq3.id, game_option_id: q3_right.id)

      # T_q3 + 2s: Alice answers WRONG (stays at 2 pts, total correct time = 5s)
      #            Eve answers WRONG (0 pts)
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: gq3.id, game_option_id: q3_wrong.id)
      game.record_answer!(player: eve, game_question_id: gq3.id, game_option_id: q3_wrong.id)

      game.finish_question!
      game.end_game!
    end

    # Expected order:
    # 1. Bob:   2 pts, 3.0s (2s on Q1 + 1s on Q3; Q2 wrong excluded)
    # 2. Alice: 2 pts, 5.0s (1s on Q1 + 4s on Q2; Q3 wrong excluded; duplicate retry on Q1 ignored)
    # 3. Dave:  1 pt,  0.5s (0.5s on Q2; 5s wrong Q1 excluded)
    # 4. Carol: 1 pt,  5.0s (5s last pick on Q1; Q2 wrong excluded)
    # 5. Eve:   0 pts, 0.0s
    board = game.leaderboard
    assert_equal [ bob.id, alice.id, dave.id, carol.id, eve.id ], board.map { |e| e[:player_id] }
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ], board.map { |e| e[:place] }
    assert_equal [ 2, 2, 1, 1, 0 ], board.map { |e| e[:points] }
    assert_equal [ false, false, false, false, false ], board.map { |e| e[:winner] }

    assert_in_delta 3_000_000, board[0][:total_time_us], 50_000
    assert_in_delta 5_000_000, board[1][:total_time_us], 50_000
    assert_in_delta   500_000, board[2][:total_time_us], 50_000
    assert_in_delta 5_000_000, board[3][:total_time_us], 50_000
    assert_equal 0, board[4][:total_time_us]

    # Verify player_state after end
    bob_state = game.player_state(bob)
    assert_equal "ended", bob_state[:status]
    assert_equal 1, bob_state[:place]
    assert_equal 5, bob_state[:total_players]
    assert_equal 2, bob_state[:points]
    assert_equal false, bob_state[:winner]

    carol_state = game.player_state(carol)
    assert_equal 4, carol_state[:place]
    assert_equal 5, carol_state[:total_players]
    assert_equal 1, carol_state[:points]
    assert_equal false, carol_state[:winner]
  end

  test "pick_top_winners!, draw_winners!, and reset_winners! respect ties, 0-point exclusion, and fewer-than-N rule" do
    @quiz.update!(number_of_winners: 3)
    game = Game.create_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    gq1, gq2, gq3 = game.game_questions.includes(:game_options).to_a

    # 6 players:
    # Alice: 3 pts
    # Bob:   2 pts (fast)
    # Carol: 2 pts (medium)
    # Dave:  2 pts (slow)
    # Eve:   1 pt
    # Frank: 0 pts
    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    bob   = game.players.create!(name: "Bob")
    carol = game.players.create!(name: "Carol")
    dave  = game.players.create!(name: "Dave")
    eve   = game.players.create!(name: "Eve")
    frank = game.players.create!(name: "Frank")

    create_correct = lambda do |player, gq, us|
      Answer.create!(
        game: game,
        player: player,
        game_question: gq,
        game_option: gq.game_options.find_by!(correct: true),
        response_time_us: us
      )
    end

    # Alice: 3 pts
    create_correct.call(alice, gq1, 1_000_000)
    create_correct.call(alice, gq2, 1_000_000)
    create_correct.call(alice, gq3, 1_000_000)

    # Bob: 2 pts, 1s total
    create_correct.call(bob, gq1, 500_000)
    create_correct.call(bob, gq2, 500_000)

    # Carol: 2 pts, 2s total
    create_correct.call(carol, gq1, 1_000_000)
    create_correct.call(carol, gq2, 1_000_000)

    # Dave: 2 pts, 4s total
    create_correct.call(dave, gq1, 2_000_000)
    create_correct.call(dave, gq2, 2_000_000)

    # Eve: 1 pt
    create_correct.call(eve, gq1, 100_000)

    # Winner actions rejected before end_game!
    assert_not game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_not game.draw_winners!
    assert_not game.reset_winners!

    game.end_game!

    # Top 3 -> Alice, Bob, Carol (by points then speed)
    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    winners = game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id).sort
    assert_equal [ alice.id, bob.id, carol.id ].sort, winners

    # Reset winners -> none
    assert game.reset_winners!
    assert_equal [], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)

    # Draw (N=3):
    # 3rd place (Carol) has 2 points.
    # > 2 points: Alice (ALWAYS wins)
    # == 2 points: Bob, Carol, Dave (2 drawn at random, speed does NOT matter!)
    # < 2 points: Eve, Frank (NEVER win)
    tied_win_counts = { bob.id => 0, carol.id => 0, dave.id => 0 }
    60.times do
      assert game.draw_winners!
      ids = game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)
      assert_equal 3, ids.size
      assert_includes ids, alice.id, "Alice (> cutoff) must always win"
      assert_not_includes ids, eve.id, "Eve (< cutoff) must never win"
      assert_not_includes ids, frank.id, "Frank (0 pts) must never win"

      tied_winners = ids - [ alice.id ]
      assert_equal 2, tied_winners.size
      tied_winners.each { |pid| tied_win_counts[pid] += 1 }
    end

    # Across 60 draws of 2 from 3, probability any one never wins is (1/3)^60 < 1e-28
    # and probability any one always wins is (2/3)^60 < 3e-11.
    tied_win_counts.each do |pid, count|
      assert count > 0, "Expected tied player #{pid} to win at least once across 60 draws"
      assert count < 60, "Expected tied player #{pid} to lose at least once across 60 draws"
    end
  end

    Answer.create!(

    assert game.reset_winners!

    # Draw -> only Alice and Bob (fewer than 3 have points, so all of them win; 0-point players excluded)
    assert game.draw_winners!

  end

  test "all 0-point players results in zero winners for Top N and Draw" do
    @quiz.update!(number_of_winners: 3)

    assert game.pick_top_winners!

    assert_equal [], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)

  test "draw with N=1 and tie at 1st place draws randomly among 1st-place tie only" do

    gq1 = game.game_questions.includes(:game_options).first

    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice")

    carol = game.players.create!(name: "Carol")

    Answer.create!(game: game, player: alice, game_question: gq1, game_option: gq1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true), response_time_us: 100_000)
    Answer.create!(game: game, player: bob, game_question: gq1, game_option: gq1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true), response_time_us: 500_000)

    game.end_game!

    # Top 1 -> Alice (faster)
    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [ alice.id ], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)

require "test_helper"

class GameScoringAndWinnersTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveSupport::Testing::TimeHelpers

  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Prizes Talk Quiz", number_of_winners: 3)

    @q1 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Q1?", active: true)
    assert @q1.save_with_options([
      { title: "Q1 Right", correct: true },
      { title: "Q1 Wrong", correct: false }
    ])

    @q2 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Q2?", active: true)
    assert @q2.save_with_options([
      { title: "Q2 Right A", correct: true },
      { title: "Q2 Right B", correct: true },
      { title: "Q2 Wrong", correct: false }
    ])

    @q3 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Q3?", active: true)
    assert @q3.save_with_options([
      { title: "Q3 Right", correct: true },
      { title: "Q3 Wrong", correct: false }
    ])
  end

  test "ranks players by points then lower total time of correct answers, using last pick time and ignoring wrong answer time" do
    base_time = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-20 10:00:00 UTC")
    game = nil
    alice = bob = carol = dave = eve = nil

    travel_to(base_time, with_usec: true) do
      game = Game.create_for_quiz!(@quiz)

      bob   = game.players.create!(name: "Bob")
      carol = game.players.create!(name: "Carol")
      dave  = game.players.create!(name: "Dave")
      eve   = game.players.create!(name: "Eve")

      q1_right = gq1.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q1 Right")
      q1_wrong = gq1.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q1 Wrong")
      q2_right_a = gq2.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q2 Right A")
      q2_right_b = gq2.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q2 Right B")
      q2_wrong = gq2.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q2 Wrong")
      q3_right = gq3.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q3 Right")
      q3_wrong = gq3.game_options.find_by!(title: "Q3 Wrong")

      # Q1 opens at T=0
      assert game.start!
      assert_in_delta base_time.to_f, gq1.reload.opened_at.to_f, 0.001

      # T+1.0s: Carol picks RIGHT early, Alice picks RIGHT

        game.record_answer!(player: carol, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
        game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      end

      # T+2.0s: Bob picks RIGHT; Alice sends duplicate retry of SAME option (keeps T+1.0s!)
      travel_to(base_time + 2.0, with_usec: true) do
        game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
        game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      end

      # T+3.0s: Carol changes to WRONG
      travel_to(base_time + 3.0, with_usec: true) do
        game.record_answer!(player: carol, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_wrong.id)
      end

      # T+5.0s: Carol changes BACK to RIGHT (her Q1 time MUST be 5.0s, NOT 1.0s!)
      # Dave picks WRONG slowly at T+5.0s (wrong answer time must NOT count!)
      travel_to(base_time + 5.0, with_usec: true) do
        game.record_answer!(player: carol, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
        game.record_answer!(player: dave, game_question_id: gq1.id, game_option_id: q1_wrong.id)

        # During question & reveal, players must NEVER see points, place, or winner
        [ alice, bob, carol, dave, eve ].each do |p|
          st = game.player_state(p)
          assert_not st.key?(:points)
          assert_not st.key?(:place)
          assert_not st.key?(:total_players)
          assert_not st.key?(:winner)
        end

        game.finish_question!
        [ alice, bob, carol, dave, eve ].each do |p|
          st = game.player_state(p)
          assert_not st.key?(:points)
          assert_not st.key?(:place)
          assert_not st.key?(:total_players)
          assert_not st.key?(:winner)
        end
      end

      # Q2 opens at T+15.0s (proves Q2 timer starts at Q2 open, not Q1 open!)
      q2_open = base_time + 15.0
      travel_to(q2_open, with_usec: true) do
        assert game.next_question!
        assert_in_delta q2_open.to_f, gq2.reload.opened_at.to_f, 0.001
      end

      # Q2 + 0.5s: Dave answers RIGHT (total correct time = 0.5s, 1 pt!)
      travel_to(q2_open + 0.5, with_usec: true) do
        game.record_answer!(player: dave, game_question_id: gq2.id, game_option_id: q2_right_b.id)
      end

      # Q2 + 4.0s: Alice answers RIGHT (total correct time = 1.0s + 4.0s = 5.0s, 2 pts)
      #            Bob answers WRONG (stays at 1 pt, total correct time = 2.0s)
      #            Carol answers WRONG (stays at 1 pt, total correct time = 5.0s)
      travel_to(q2_open + 4.0, with_usec: true) do
        game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: gq2.id, game_option_id: q2_right_a.id)
        game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: gq2.id, game_option_id: q2_wrong.id)
        game.record_answer!(player: carol, game_question_id: gq2.id, game_option_id: q2_wrong.id)
        game.finish_question!
      end

      # Q3 opens at T+25.0s
      q3_open = base_time + 25.0
      travel_to(q3_open, with_usec: true) do
        assert game.next_question!
      end

      # Q3 + 1.25s: Bob answers RIGHT (total 2 pts, total correct time = 2.0s + 1.25s = 3.25s -> FASTER than Alice's 5.0s!)

        game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: gq3.id, game_option_id: q3_right.id)
      end

      # Q3 + 2.0s: Alice answers WRONG (stays at 2 pts, total correct time = 5.0s)

    assert game.reset_winners!
    assert_equal [], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)

    # Draw -> only Alice and Bob (fewer than 3 have points, so all of them win; 0-point players excluded)
    assert game.draw_winners!
    assert_equal [ alice.id, bob.id ].sort, game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "all 0-point players results in zero winners for Top N and Draw" do
    @quiz.update!(number_of_winners: 3)
    game = Game.create_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    game.players.create!(name: "Bob")
    game.end_game!

    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)

    assert game.draw_winners!
    assert_equal [], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)
  end

  test "draw with N=1 and tie at 1st place draws randomly among 1st-place tie only" do
    @quiz.update!(number_of_winners: 1)
    game = Game.create_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    gq1 = game.game_questions.includes(:game_options).first

    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    bob   = game.players.create!(name: "Bob")

    Answer.create!(game: game, player: alice, game_question: gq1, game_option: gq1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true), response_time_us: 100_000)
    Answer.create!(game: game, player: bob, game_question: gq1, game_option: gq1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true), response_time_us: 500_000)

    game.end_game!

    # Top 1 -> Alice (faster)
    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [ alice.id ], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)

    # Draw -> randomly Alice or Bob, never Carol (0 pts)
    seen = Set.new
    40.times do
      assert game.draw_winners!
      ids = game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)
      assert_equal 1, ids.size
      assert_not_includes ids, carol.id
      seen << ids.first
    end
    assert_equal [ alice.id, bob.id ].sort, seen.to_a.sort
  end

  test "duplicate player names are ranked and awarded winners independently by player id" do
    @quiz.update!(number_of_winners: 1)
    game = Game.create_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    gq1 = game.game_questions.includes(:game_options).first

    alex1 = game.players.create!(name: "Alex")

    Answer.create!(game: game, player: alex2, game_question: gq1, game_option: gq1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true), response_time_us: 500_000)

    game.end_game!
    assert game.pick_top_winners!

    assert_equal 1, game.player_state(alex2)[:place]
    assert_equal true, game.player_state(alex2)[:winner]
    assert_equal 2, game.player_state(alex1)[:place]
    assert_equal false, game.player_state(alex1)[:winner]
  end
end

**System Test Strategy: Prize and Leaderboard Functionality**

Okay, here's the game plan. The existing test suite passed, so now it's time to build out some comprehensive system tests for the prize and leaderboard functionality. I need to make sure this is rock solid. I'll be driving actual Chromium browsers using the system tests. This will be an end-to-end test, driving the moderator's big screen and multiple player phones simultaneously.

First, I'll focus on the quiz settings, specifically the `"Number of winners"` field. I'll need to check the default value of `3`, and make sure validation is correct: that it rejects inputs like `0`, `-1`, and empty fields. I'll need to verify that valid values (e.g., `2`) are persisted correctly and that the "Top N" button updates dynamically based on the input.

Next, the meat of the tests: a full live multi-phone game. This means:

*   **Simultaneous Delivery:** I'll confirm that questions are delivered near-instantaneously to both the big screen and the phones. Latency needs to be under 1.5 seconds, without any forced reloads.
*   **Point Visibility:** Players *shouldn't* see their points during the lobby, the question phase, or the reveal phase. Points are revealed on the leaderboard.
*   **Scoring Accuracy:** I'll verify the scoring logic: 1 point per correct answer, speed tie-breaking based on total time of *correct* answers, and that changing answers adds time, making the player slower.
*   **"End Quiz" Results:** After the quiz ends, I'll need to confirm that the big screen leaderboard (`<ol class="leaderboard">`) is displayed correctly, with each player's place, name, and score, in the correct order. I need to assert that no extraneous or hidden `<li>`s are lingering. Every phone must *also* update live, without a page reload, showing "Place X of Y" and the player's correct score in singular or plural ("1 point", "2 points", or "0 points").
*   **"Top N" Winner Designation:** The "Top N" button should correctly mark the first N eligible players as "Winner" on the leaderboard and show "You won!" LIVE on their phones. Non-winners need to *not* have the "Winner" or "You won!" indicators.
*   **Persistence and Live Updates:** I need to thoroughly test page reload persistence on both the big screen and the phones, and then verify that live updates still work on reloaded phones after the moderator interacts with the "Reset winners" and "Draw" buttons.
*   **"Reset Winners" Functionality:** The "Reset winners" button should remove the "Winner" designation from the leaderboard and remove "You won!" from the phones *live*.
*   **"Draw" Functionality:** The "Draw" button will need to test the logic to make sure the winner designation works as expected in a draw scenario. Specifically, I'll need to verify that players with more points than the N-th place are *always* winners, players with 0 points or fewer are *never* winners, and remaining prizes are drawn randomly from the tied pool. I'll confirm that each click redraws the winners and updates both the leaderboard and phones LIVE.
*   **Edge Cases for "Draw":** I need to cover edge cases: fewer than N players with points (all win), 0-point players (never win), and 0 players joined (clean empty state).
*   **Second Big Screen:** I'll also ensure that a second big screen window updates live on `"End quiz"`, `"Top N"`, `"Draw"`, and `"Reset winners"`.

Alright, I'll start with creating `test/system/prizes_and_leaderboard_system_test.rb` and get those system tests up and running with `bin/rails test:system`. This is going to be a deep dive.

require "application_system_test_case"

class PrizesAndLeaderboardSystemTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  test "quiz settings Number of winners defaults to 3, validates >= 1, and updates Top N label" do
    visit "/moderate"
    click_on "New quiz"

    assert_field "Number of winners", with: "3"

    # Rejects 0 and negative values
    fill_in "Title", with: "Prizes Settings Quiz"
    fill_in "Number of winners", with: "0"
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_selector ".errors[role='alert']"
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.count

    fill_in "Number of winners", with: "-2"
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_selector ".errors[role='alert']"
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.count

    fill_in "Number of winners", with: ""
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_selector ".errors[role='alert']"
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.count

    # Create with default 3
    fill_in "Number of winners", with: "3"
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_selector "h1", text: "Prizes Settings Quiz"
    quiz = Quiz.last
    assert_equal 3, quiz.number_of_winners

    # Edit via Settings to 2
    click_link "Settings"
    assert_field "Number of winners", with: "3"

    fill_in "Number of winners", with: "0"
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_selector ".errors[role='alert']"
    assert_equal 3, quiz.reload.number_of_winners

    fill_in "Number of winners", with: "2"
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_selector "h1", text: "Prizes Settings Quiz"
    assert_equal 2, quiz.reload.number_of_winners
  end

  test "scoring, speed tie-breaking, last-pick timing, instant sync, leaderboard, Top N, Draw, and Reset winners update live" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Speed & Prizes Conf", number_of_winners: 2)

    q1 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Capital of Japan?", active: true)
    assert q1.save_with_options([
      { title: "Tokyo", correct: true },
      { title: "Kyoto", correct: false }
    ])

    q2 = quiz.questions.build(body: "HTTP OK status?", active: true)
    assert q2.save_with_options([
      { title: "200", correct: true },
      { title: "404", correct: false }
    ])

    visit moderate_quiz_path(quiz)
    click_button "Start a game"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip

    # 5 players join on separate phones
    %i[alice bob carol dave eve].each do |sym|
      name = sym.to_s.capitalize
      Capybara.using_session(sym) do
        visit join_url
        fill_in "Your name", with: name
        click_button "Join"
        assert_text "Hi, #{name}!"
        assert_no_text "point"
      end
    end

    assert_text "Players: 5"

    # Open Q1 and verify all 5 phones receive it close to instantly (no reload)
    t_start = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    click_button "Start"
    assert_text "Capital of Japan?"

    %i[alice bob carol dave eve].each do |sym|
      Capybara.using_session(sym) do
        assert_text "Capital of Japan?", wait: 2
        assert_no_text "point"
      end
    end
    elapsed_sync = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t_start
    assert elapsed_sync < 3.0, "Expected all 5 phones to receive Q1 close to instantly, took #{elapsed_sync.round(2)}s"

    # Q1 picks with controlled ordering:
    # 1. Alice picks RIGHT immediately (fast!)
    # 2. Carol picks RIGHT immediately (will switch later so last-pick makes her slower!)
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) { click_button "Tokyo" }
    Capybara.using_session(:carol) { click_button "Tokyo" }
    assert_text "Answers: 2 / 5"

    # Pause so Bob's Q1 correct time is clearly slower than Alice's, and Carol's last pick is slower than Bob's
    sleep 0.25
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) { click_button "Tokyo" }
    assert_text "Answers: 3 / 5"

    sleep 0.25
    # Carol switches to WRONG then back to RIGHT -> last pick resets Carol's Q1 timer!
    Capybara.using_session(:carol) do
      click_button "Kyoto"
      within("button.play-option", text: "Kyoto") { assert_text "Your answer" }
      sleep 0.15
      click_button "Tokyo"
      within("button.play-option", text: "Tokyo") { assert_text "Your answer" }
    end

    # Dave picks WRONG very late (wrong answer time must NOT count toward Dave's speed!)
    sleep 0.35
    Capybara.using_session(:dave) { click_button "Kyoto" }
    assert_text "Answers: 4 / 5"

    # Finish Q1 -> reveal; players still MUST NOT see points!
    click_button "Finish"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Correct!"
      assert_no_text "point"
      assert_no_text "Place"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:dave) do
      assert_text "Wrong!"
      assert_no_text "point"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:eve) do
      assert_text "No answer"
      assert_no_text "point"
    end

    # Open Q2 -> instant delivery to all phones
    click_button "Next"
    assert_text "HTTP OK status?"
    %i[alice bob carol dave eve].each do |sym|
      Capybara.using_session(sym) do
        assert_text "HTTP OK status?", wait: 2
        assert_no_text "point"
      end
    end

    # Q2 picks:
    # Dave answers RIGHT immediately (very fast! 1 pt total, faster than Bob & Carol's Q1 correct times!)
    # Alice answers RIGHT (2 pts total!)
    Capybara.using_session(:dave) { click_button "200" }
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) { click_button "200" }
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) { click_button "404" }
    Capybara.using_session(:carol) { click_button "404" }
    Capybara.using_session(:eve) { click_button "404" }
    assert_text "Answers: 5 / 5"

    click_button "Finish"
    assert_button "End quiz"

    # Open a second moderator big screen window to verify projector live sync too
    projector = open_new_window
    within_window(projector) do
      visit current_path
      assert_text "HTTP OK status?"
    end

    # End quiz!
    click_button "End quiz"

    # Big screen shows ONLY the 5 leaderboard list items in exact order:
    # 1. Alice (2 points)
    # 2. Dave  (1 point - fast Q2; slow wrong Q1 ignored!)
    # 3. Bob   (1 point - faster Q1 than Carol)
    # 4. Carol (1 point - slowest due to last-pick change on Q1)
    # 5. Eve   (0 points)
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li", count: 5
    assert_selector "li", count: 5, visible: :all # No lingering hidden question option <li>s!

    items = all("ol.leaderboard > li")
    expected_rows = [
      [ "1", "Alice", "2 points" ],
      [ "2", "Dave",  "1 point" ],
      [ "3", "Bob",   "1 point" ],
      [ "4", "Carol", "1 point" ],
      [ "5", "Eve",   "0 points" ]
    ]
    expected_rows.each_with_index do |(place, name, pts), idx|
      within(items[idx]) do
        assert_selector ".leader__place", exact_text: place
        assert_text name
        assert_text pts
        assert_no_text "Winner"
      end
    end

    assert_button "Top 2"
    assert_button "Draw"
    assert_button "Reset winners"

    # Second big screen (projector) updated LIVE
    within_window(projector) do
      assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li", count: 5
      assert_text "Alice"
    end

    # All 5 phones updated LIVE without reload!
    expected_phones = {
      alice: [ "Place 1 of 5", "2 points" ],
      dave:  [ "Place 2 of 5", "1 point" ],
      bob:   [ "Place 3 of 5", "1 point" ],
      carol: [ "Place 4 of 5", "1 point" ],
      eve:   [ "Place 5 of 5", "0 points" ]
    }
    expected_phones.each do |sym, (place_text, points_text)|
      Capybara.using_session(sym) do
        assert_text place_text
        assert_text points_text
        assert_no_text "You won!"
      end
    end

    # Click "Top 2" -> Alice and Dave win LIVE on big screen, projector, and phones!
    click_button "Top 2"

    within(all("ol.leaderboard > li")[0]) { assert_text "Alice"; assert_text "Winner" }
    within(all("ol.leaderboard > li")[1]) { assert_text "Dave";  assert_text "Winner" }
    within(all("ol.leaderboard > li")[2]) { assert_text "Bob";   assert_no_text "Winner" }
    within(all("ol.leaderboard > li")[3]) { assert_text "Carol"; assert_no_text "Winner" }
    within(all("ol.leaderboard > li")[4]) { assert_text "Eve";   assert_no_text "Winner" }

    within_window(projector) do
      assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner", count: 2
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) { assert_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:dave)  { assert_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:bob)   { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:carol) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:eve)   { assert_no_text "You won!" }

    # Reload Alice's phone, Carol's phone, and big screen -> state persists AND live updates continue!
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      visit join_url
      assert_text "Place 1 of 5"
      assert_text "2 points"
      assert_text "You won!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:carol) do
      visit join_url
      assert_text "Place 4 of 5"
      assert_text "1 point"
      assert_no_text "You won!"
    end
    visit current_path
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner", count: 2

    # Click "Reset winners" -> clears all winners LIVE everywhere (including reloaded phones!)
    click_button "Reset winners"
    assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner"
    assert_no_text "Winner"
    within_window(projector) { assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner" }

    %i[alice bob carol dave eve].each do |sym|
      Capybara.using_session(sym) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    end

    # Click "Draw" multiple times:
    # N = 2. 2nd place (Dave) has 1 point.
    # > 1 pt: Alice (ALWAYS wins)
    # == 1 pt: Dave, Bob, Carol (1 drawn at random; speed doesn't matter!)
    # 0 pts: Eve (NEVER wins)
    seen_tied_winners = Set.new
    15.times do
      click_button "Draw"
      assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner", count: 2

      winner_names = all("ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner .leader__name-text").map(&:text)
      assert_equal 2, winner_names.size
      assert_includes winner_names, "Alice"
      assert_not_includes winner_names, "Eve"

      assert_includes %w[Dave Bob Carol], tied_winner

      %i[alice dave bob carol eve].each do |sym|

        Capybara.using_session(sym) do
          if winner_names.include?(name)
            assert_text "You won!"
          else
            assert_no_text "You won!"
          end
        end
      end

      break if seen_tied_winners.size >= 2
    end

    assert seen_tied_winners.size >= 2, "Expected Draw to randomly pick different tied players across clicks, only saw #{seen_tied_winners.to_a}"

    projector.close
  end

  test "0-point players never win and fewer than N scorers all win" do

    within(all("ol.leaderboard > li")[0]) { assert_text "Alice"; assert_text "1 point"; assert_text "Winner" }
    within(all("ol.leaderboard > li")[1]) { assert_text "0 points"; assert_no_text "Winner" }
    within(all("ol.leaderboard > li")[2]) { assert_text "0 points"; assert_no_text "Winner" }

    Capybara.using_session(:sparse_alice) { assert_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:sparse_bob)   { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:sparse_carol) { assert_no_text "You won!" }

    # Reset -> nobody wins
    click_button "Reset winners"
    assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner"
    Capybara.using_session(:sparse_alice) { assert_no_text "You won!" }

    # Draw -> ONLY Alice wins (fewer than 3 have points, so all of them win; 0-point players never win)
    click_button "Draw"
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner", count: 1
    Capybara.using_session(:sparse_alice) { assert_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:sparse_bob)   { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:sparse_carol) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
  end

  test "all 0-point players produces zero winners and empty game ends cleanly" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Zero Point Quiz", number_of_winners: 3)
    q1 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Pick right", active: true)
    assert q1.save_with_options([
      { title: "Yes", correct: true },
      { title: "No", correct: false }
    ])

    # Game with 2 players who both score 0
    visit moderate_quiz_path(quiz)
    click_button "Start a game"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip

    Capybara.using_session(:zero_a) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "ZeroA"
      click_button "Join"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:zero_b) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "ZeroB"
      click_button "Join"
    end

    assert_text "Players: 2"
    click_button "Start"
    Capybara.using_session(:zero_a) { click_button "No" }
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"
    click_button "Finish"
    click_button "End quiz"

    click_button "Top 3"
    assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner"
    assert_no_text "Winner"
    Capybara.using_session(:zero_a) { assert_text "0 points"; assert_no_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:zero_b) { assert_text "0 points"; assert_no_text "You won!" }

    click_button "Draw"
    assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner"
    assert_no_text "Winner"

    # Game with 0 players ends cleanly and winner buttons are safe no-ops
    visit moderate_quiz_path(quiz)
    click_button "Start a game"
    click_button "Start"
    click_button "Finish"
    click_button "End quiz"

    assert_text "The quiz is over"
    assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li"
    click_button "Top 3"
    click_button "Draw"
    click_button "Reset winners"
    assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li"
  end
end

class GameChannelsTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase

    self.class.tests ModeratorGameChannel

    subscribe
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(token: "forged-token")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    self.class.tests PlayerGameChannel

    assert subscription.rejected?

    @game.start!
    subscribe(token: @player.stream_token, tab_id: "tab-a")
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream Game.players_stream_name(@game.id)
    assert_has_stream Game.player_stream_name(@game.id, @player.id)
